mainTopic: Reserving land in a gift, the meaning of 'כל שהוא', how wording defines movables, and whether a slave counts as land or movable property
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a debate between אביי and רב יוסף about a שכיב מרע who gave everything away but kept 'any amount of land' (קרקע כל שהוא). אביי cites רבי אלעזר, who says movables count as a reservation in the case of a slave. רב יוסף answers that the word 'land' in the slave משנה was only borrowed from רבי עקיבא's earlier clause. אביי then shows that 'כל שהוא' has a minimum in the case of ראשית הגז. רב יוסף answers that there the חכמים used the phrase only to contrast with רבי דוסא's larger amount. Next the גמרא lists three ways of wording a gift of movables: 'my movables', 'all my movables', and 'everything that moves'. Each wording includes more items than the one before. Then the גמרא asks whether a slave counts as land or as movable property. A proof from the משנה about selling a city is pushed away, because a slave is 'property that walks' in either category. רבינא brings a second proof from רבי אלעזר's rule, and רב נחמן explains that rule by saying outright that a slave is movable property.

steps.title: Movable property counts as a reservation for a slave
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף using רבי אלעזר's rule. Movable property counts as a 'reservation' when a master gives his property to his slave. It does not count when a husband reserves property for his wife's כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב דימי בר יוסף said in the name of רבי אלעזר: The חכמים treated movable property as a reservation in the case of a slave. They did not treat movable property as a reservation in the case of a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues an attack on רב יוסף. רב יוסף had said that only land counts as a 'reservation,' and here a statement of רבי אלעזר is brought that seems to disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about a slave also says 'he reserved any amount of land,' yet רבי אלעזר says movables work there too. That suggests the word 'land' in such a משנה is not exact. If so, our משנה's 'land' should not exclude movables either, which goes against רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable property, anything that can be carried, as opposed to land
A reservation: property the giver holds back for himself
A slave. If his master writes all his property to him, he goes free, unless the master reserved something
A wife's marriage contract and the money it promises her

steps.confusionAlert: The two halves point in opposite directions. For a slave, movables DO count as a reservation, so he does not go free. For a כתובה, movables do NOT count, so the wife does not lose her כתובה. Only the slave half is the challenge against רב יוסף.

phrases.english: And Rav Dimi bar Yosef said
that Rabbi Elazar said:
They made movable property a reservation in the case of a slave,
phrases.notes: So if the master gave the slave everything except some movables, the slave does not go free.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עָשׂוּ מְטַלְטְלִין שִׁיּוּר אֵצֶל כְּתוּבָּה!
phrases.english: but they did not make movable property a reservation in the case of a כתובה!
phrases.notes: If a husband gave everything to his sons and left his wife only movables, she does not lose her כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's challenge to רב יוסף's claim that only land counts as a reservation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reading that the word 'קרקע' in the משנה excludes movable property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The slave משנה also says 'land,' yet movables work there. So 'land' is not exact, and it should not be exact in our משנה either.

steps.title: The word 'land' in the slave case was borrowed from the earlier clause
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the slave משנה really should not have said 'land.' It said 'land' only because the clause before it, רבי עקיבא's list of laws, was about land.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it really should not have said 'land.' But since the first clause taught that רבי עקיבא says any amount of land is obligated in פאה and ביכורים, lets one write a פרוזבול, and lets one acquire movables together with it by money, document, or taking possession, it says 'land' in the slave case as well.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself. He says that the word 'land' in the slave משנה is just a carry-over from the clause before it, so no lesson can be learned from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי עקיבא's clause, land is truly needed for every law listed. The slave clause simply kept the same wording, so movables really do work there. That is no proof about our משנה, where רב יוסף still holds that 'land' is meant exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: By right; strictly speaking, it should have been this way
Since the first clause taught it; the wording is copied from earlier
A document that keeps the שמיטה year from canceling a loan
Property that is not a guarantee for debts; movables
Money, a document, and taking possession: the three ways land is acquired

steps.whyThisMatters: This 'אַיְּידִי' answer is a common tool across ש״ס: a word in a משנה may be there only for style or parallel wording, not to teach a law.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם בְּדִין הוּא דְּלָא לִיתְנֵי קַרְקַע;
phrases.english: There, by right it should not have taught 'land';
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה about the slave.

phrases.english: but since the first clause taught:
Rabbi Akiva says:
Land of any amount
is obligated in פאה and in ביכורים,
and one may write a פרוזבול on it,
phrases.notes: A פרוזבול works only if the borrower owns some land, and here even a tiny piece is enough.

phrases.aramaic: וְלִקְנוֹת עִמָּהֶם נְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת
phrases.english: and one may acquire movable property together with it
by money, by a document, or by taking possession –
because of this it teaches 'land' in the slave case too.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּדִין הוּא דְּלָא לִיתְנֵי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי אלעזר's rule about a slave.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording explanation: the word was carried over from the previous clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'land' in the slave משנה is exact, so 'land' in such a משנה never excludes movables.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the slave משנה, 'land' is only borrowed wording. In our משנה, 'land' can still be exact.

steps.title: 'Any amount' sometimes has a minimum: the case of ראשית הגז
steps.stepSummary: אביי now challenges רב יוסף's second claim, that 'כל שהוא' means truly any amount. In the laws of ראשית הגז, the חכמים say 'כל שהן,' yet רב explains that this means a set minimum.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whenever it says 'any amount,' is there no minimum? But we learned: רבי דוסא בן הרכינס says that five sheep each sheared for a מנה and a half obligate the owner in ראשית הגז. The חכמים say five sheep sheared for any amount. And we asked: how much is 'any amount'? רב said: a מנה and a half in total, as long as it is split evenly among the five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attack on רב יוסף. It brings a משנה where 'any amount' turns out to have a fixed minimum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that 'כל שהוא' in our משנה means even the tiniest bit of land. But in ראשית הגז, 'כל שהן' means a real total of 150 דינרים. So perhaps 'כל שהוא' in our משנה also hides a minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even the smallest
A set measure or minimum amount
The first shearing: wool that must be given to a כהן
A מנה (100 דינרים) and a half, so 150 דינרים in weight
Divided into five, so each sheep gives an equal share

phrases.english: And wherever it teaches 'any amount' –
does it have no minimum measure?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says:
Five sheep that are sheared
for a מנה and a half each –
are obligated in the first shearing.
And the Sages say:
Five sheep sheared for any amount.
And we said: And how much is 'any amount'?
Rav said: a מנה and a half,
phrases.notes: This time it is 150 in total for all five sheep, not 150 for each one.

phrases.english: provided that they are divided equally among the five!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּתָנֵי כׇּל שֶׁהוּא לֵית לֵיהּ שִׁיעוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the land-versus-movables issue and attacks the meaning of 'כל שהוא.'
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that 'כל שהוא' in our משנה means literally any amount.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In ראשית הגז, the phrase 'כל שהן' really has a minimum of 150 דינרים. So the phrase does not always mean the tiniest amount.

steps.title: There 'any amount' only contrasts with a bigger amount
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that in ראשית הגז the חכמים should not really have said 'any amount.' They used the phrase only because רבי דוסא gave a large measure, so their smaller measure was called 'any amount' by contrast.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, by right it should not have said 'any amount.' But since the first תנא stated a large measure, they also stated a small measure and called it 'any amount.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains away the ראשית הגז case. He says that the phrase was used there as a contrast, not as a literal description.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים were responding to רבי דוסא's large number, so they described their own smaller number as 'כל שהן.' In our משנה nobody is being answered, so 'כל שהוא' keeps its plain meaning of truly any amount of land.

keyTerms.meaning: The first opinion stated in a משנה
A large measure
A small measure

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף holds his ground on both points. The word 'land' in the slave משנה was only borrowed wording, and 'any amount' in ראשית הגז was only a contrast. In our משנה both words can be read exactly: land only, and any amount at all.

phrases.english: There, by right
it should not have taught 'any amount';

phrases.aramaic: וְאַיְּידֵי דְּקָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא שִׁיעוּרָא רַבָּה,
phrases.english: but since the first תנא stated a large measure,
phrases.notes: The first תנא is רבי דוסא, with his 150 דינרים for each sheep.

phrases.english: they too stated a small measure –
and they called it 'any amount.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּדִין הוּא דְּלָא לִיתְנֵי כׇּל שֶׁהוּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording explanation: the phrase was used as a contrast to the other opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כל שהוא' can mean a hidden minimum, so our משנה might need a minimum amount of land too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only in ראשית הגז was the phrase used loosely, as a contrast. In our משנה, 'כל שהוא' means literally any amount.

steps.title: Three ways of wording a gift of movable property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states as obvious that the exact wording of a gift decides which movable items are included: 'my movables', 'all my movables', or 'everything that moves'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if someone says 'My movable property goes to so-and-so', the receiver gets all his everyday utensils, but not his wheat and barley. If he says 'All my movable property', the receiver gets even the wheat and barley, and even the upper millstone, but not the lower millstone. If he says 'Everything that can be moved', the receiver gets even the lower millstone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out three levels of wording for a gift of movables. Each wording covers more items than the one before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain 'מטלטלי' means the things a person uses day to day, so stored grain is left out. Adding 'כל' widens it to every movable item, even the upper millstone, which does get lifted. 'כל דמטלטל' means anything that physically can be moved, so even the heavy lower millstone is included.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
Movable property
His everyday utensils
The upper millstone, which is sometimes lifted off
The lower millstone, which basically stays in place

phrases.english: It is obvious: if he said, 'My movable property to so-and-so,'
he acquires all his everyday utensils,
except for wheat and barley.
'All my movable property to so-and-so':
even wheat and barley.
And he acquires even the upper millstone,
phrases.notes: The upper millstone gets lifted off now and then, so it counts as something that moves.

phrases.english: except for the lower millstone.
'Everything that can be moved':
he acquires even the lower millstone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the רב יוסף and אביי exchange to a new set of wording rules about movable property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'מטלטלי' covers everyday utensils only; 'כל מטלטלי' covers all movables except the lower millstone; 'כל דמטלטל' covers even the lower millstone.

steps.title: Is a slave treated like land or like movable property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a question: does an עבד כנעני have the legal status of land or of movable property?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: is a slave considered like land, or like movable property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about how to classify a slave. This sets up the proofs that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave moves on his own, like movable property. But in some areas of הלכה he is treated like land. The question is which category he belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them (the חכמים)
A slave (here an עבד כנעני)
Land
Is considered like, is similar to

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Is a slave like land
or is he like movable property?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עַבְדָּא – כִּמְקַרְקְעָא אוֹ כְּמִטַּלְטְלָא דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining movable property, the גמרא asks where a slave fits.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a slave has the legal status of land or of movable property.

steps.title: Proof from selling a city: a slave seems like movable property
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא brings the משנה about selling a city. Slaves are not included in a plain sale of the city, which suggests they are like movable property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב אויא said to רב אשי: Come and hear: One who sells a city has sold the houses, ditches, caves, bathhouses, olive presses and irrigated fields, but not the movable property. But if he said 'the city and everything in it', even animals or slaves in it are all sold. This makes sense if a slave is like movable property: that is why he is not sold in the first case. But if a slave is like land, why is he not sold along with the city?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא tries to answer the question using the משנה about selling a city. He argues that a slave must be like movable property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a plain sale, all the land-type parts of the city are sold, but movables are not. Slaves are sold only when the seller adds 'everything in it'. If slaves were like land, they should have been sold in the plain sale too, so they must be like movables.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sells the city
It makes sense, granted
Is sold
The first part of the משנה

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Avya said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear:
One who sells the city
has sold the houses, ditches, caves, and bathhouses,
the olive presses, and the irrigated fields;
but not the movable property.
But when he said: 'It and everything that is in it,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הָיוּ בָּהּ בְּהֵמָה אוֹ עֲבָדִים –
phrases.english: even if there were animals or slaves in it,
they are all sold.
It makes sense if you say he is like movable property:
that is why he is not sold in the first case;
but if you say he is like land,
why is he not sold?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הָעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proof to settle the question from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That a slave is like movable property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about selling a city: slaves are not included in a plain sale, only when 'everything in it' is said.

steps.title: The city proof fails: a slave is 'land that moves'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the proof does not work. Even if a slave is like land, he is land that walks, so he may not go with the city in a plain sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what then, is he like movable property?! Then why does the משנה say 'even' slaves are sold? You must say that movable property that moves on its own is different from movable property that does not move. In the same way, even if a slave is like land, land that moves is different from land that does not move.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes away רב אחא's proof. He shows the משנה fits both views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אפילו' (even) in the משנה shows slaves are a special case even among movables, because they walk on their own. If walking makes slaves special among movables, it can also make them special among land. So the plain sale may leave slaves out even if they are like land.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, what (would you say)?
Is different
Moves (on its own)
Even (a word that signals a new point)

phrases.english: But rather, what? Is he like movable property?!
Then what is the 'even'?
phrases.notes: If slaves were just plain movables, the משנה would not need to say 'even' slaves are sold.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
phrases.notes: Some versions add the word in square brackets here.

phrases.english: Movable property that moves on its own is different
from movable property that does not move;
so even if you say he is like land,
land that moves is different
from land that does not move.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the city משנה. This proof does not settle the question from step 6; רבינא tries a new proof in step 9.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'even' in the משנה shows slaves are special because they move on their own. That fact explains their exclusion whether they are like land or like movables.
steps.whatToRemember: The city משנה cannot decide the question, because a slave is a unique 'moving' kind of property in either category.

steps.title: A new proof from the משנה about writing all property to a slave
steps.stepSummary: רבינא begins a new proof from the משנה where a master writes all his property to his slave. Reserving any land stops the slave from going free, but רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Come and hear: One who writes all his property to his slave, the slave goes out free. If he reserved any amount of land, the slave does not go free. רבי שמעון says: He is always free, unless the master says 'All my property is given to so-and-so my slave, except for one ten-thousandth of it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא quotes a משנה as a new proof about whether a slave is like land. This step only quotes the source; the argument from it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a reserved piece of land stops the slave from going free, perhaps because the master may have kept the slave too. רבינא will try to use this to show how a slave is classified. רבי שמעון holds that the slave goes free even if the master kept back some land. He stays a slave only if the master holds back an unspecified share of everything, like 'one ten-thousandth'.

keyTerms.meaning: One who writes (gives by a document)
A free man
He reserved, kept back
Ten thousand

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear:
One who writes all his property to his slave,
the slave goes out a free man.
If he reserved any amount of land,
he does not go out a free man.
Rabbi Shimon says:
He is always a free man,
unless he says:
'All my property is given to so-and-so my slave,
except for one ten-thousandth of it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע, הַכּוֹתֵב לְעַבְדּוֹ כׇּל נְכָסָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a second proof for the question in step 6 begins.
steps.raayaObject: The status of a slave, land or movable property (the argument itself comes next).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פאה about a master who writes all his property to his slave.

steps.title: Holding back movables counts for a slave but not for a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that keeping back movable items is a real שיור when giving property to a slave, but not in the case of a wife's כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי בר יוסף said in the name of רבי אלעזר: The חכמים treated movable property as a real 'holding back' when it comes to a slave, but they did not treat movable property as a real 'holding back' when it comes to a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי אלעזר as the next part of רבינא's proof. It is setting up the question of why movables count as holding back in one case and not in the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, the רבנן said that if a master holds back any land, the slave does not go free. Now רבי אלעזר adds that even holding back movable items stops the slave from going free. But in the כתובה case, holding back movables does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding something back; keeping part of the property for yourself
Movable property
A wife's marriage contract and the money it promises her
A slave (here, an עבד כנעני)

phrases.english: And Rav Dimi bar Yosef said
that Rabbi Elazar said:
They made movable property count as holding back with regard to a slave,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עָשׂוּ מִטַּלְטְלִין שִׁיּוּר אֵצֶל כְּתוּבָּה.
phrases.english: but they did not make movable property count as holding back with regard to a כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבינא's proof by adding a ruling about holding back movables
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keeping back movables counts as a real שיור for a slave, but not for a כתובה.

steps.title: רבא asks for the reason behind the difference
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן why movables count as holding back for a slave but not for a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks why the two cases are treated differently. This sets up the answer that will finish רבינא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are about holding back part of one's property, so we would expect the same rule. רבא wants to know what makes them different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: And Rava said to Rav Nachman:
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי אלעזר's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why movables count as שיור for a slave but not for a כתובה

steps.title: A slave is movable property, but a כתובה is tied to land
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains: a slave is movable, so movables can be held back against him; a כתובה is collected from land, so movables do not count as holding back against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A slave is movable property, and movables held back against movables count as a holding back. But a wife's כתובה is land, and movables held back against land do not count as a holding back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's question. In doing so he states outright that a slave is movable property, which completes רבינא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding something back only counts if it is the same kind of thing as what is being given. A slave is movable, so holding back movables counts. A כתובה is paid from land, so holding back movables does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Land; real estate
The slave

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, an עבד כנעני has the status of movable property. That is why holding back movables counts as a שיור when giving property to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the question from step 6: רבינא's proof shows that a slave is treated like movable property.
